transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-02
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Avery Kim (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Maria Gomez (Lyndon Head of ML), Thomas Reed (Cloud Infra Lead), Elaine Park (CISO)

Summary: Lyndon Bank is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for production LLM inference. They want reserved GPU pools, strict network isolation (VPC, private control plane), ability to burst to additional capacity, predictable throughput for daytime peak traffic, and enterprise security docs. Next: pricing/SOW, benchmark run, sample traffic.

00:00:00 - Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining 
can you confirm audio?
00:00:04 - Maria: Yep, we can hear you. Thanks for doing this.
00:00:08 - Avery: Awesome. Quick intros? I'm Avery, AE on Redwood. With me is Ravi, our solutions engineer.
00:00:15 - Ravi: Hey all. I'll dive into sizing and performance stuff.
00:00:18 - Maria: Hi, Maria. I run the ML team at Lyndon.
00:00:21 - Thomas: Thomas, cloud infra. We own deployment and networking.
00:00:24 - Elaine: Elaine, CISO. I'll be looking at compliance, keys, and audit.
00:00:28 - Avery: Great. Agenda: understand your current stack and workload, isolation needs, traffic patterns and bursts, then we can talk about Dedicated configs and next steps.
00:00:38 - Thomas: Quick context 
we run most infra on GCP and have a mix of on-prem for some sensitive data. We're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private. For production we lean toward dedicated or private because of data isolation and predictable cost.
00:00:53 - Maria: Our main use case is real-time document summarization and customer chat routing 
mostly shorter conversations but occasional long-context analysis for compliance requests. Latency target is sub-200ms 95p for short prompts, and we want stable throughput during business hours.
00:01:07 - Ravi: Sub-200ms 95p is fairly aggressive depending on model & batch strategy. Are you using a specific open model today?
00:01:12 - Maria: We're prototyping with an Llama-3-70b family quantized variant; some tests on Mistral. We're open to Redwood's curated models.
00:01:20 - Avery: Cool. Two immediate questions: what's your expected QPS at peak and how tolerant are you to cold-start latency for KV cache?
00:01:28 - Thomas: For peak we see about 120 QPS across all frontends, spiking to 220 QPS for a few hours when reports generate. Cold-starts are okay up to a second for background jobs, but for interactive chat we need the low tail latency.
00:01:40 - Ravi: So we should size for baseline 150 QPS with headroom for spikes to 250 QPS. That suggests reserved GPU pool with burst to additional nodes. Redwood Dedicated supports reserved pools plus burst capacity 
you can keep a minimum reserved set and allow burst to shared capacity or dedicated excess capacity.
00:01:56 - Maria: How does burst work? Is it automatic? And what about data isolation 
when bursting do requests leave our VPC?
00:02:03 - Ravi: Good question. For Dedicated, burst can be configured in two ways: within your reserved cluster (scale up within your private pool if you configured burstable nodes) or we can route to a separate dedicated overflow pool that is still isolated to your account but may be in a different AZ. For Private (VPC on-prem) you can enforce that no traffic leaves your network. If bursting to Redwood-hosted overflow, we encrypt in transit and maintain tenancy separation, but Elaine might want private-only bursts for compliance.
00:02:28 - Elaine: We prefer no egress outside our network for any PII. Are there options to keep bursts within our VPC or enable private peering?
00:02:35 - Ravi: Yes, we support VPC peering and private interconnect for Dedicated + Private setups depending on region. Also can do an on-prem private control plane for full isolation. For strictly no-egress requirements, Private on-prem deployment is the recommended path.
00:02:47 - Thomas: What's the typical reserved GPU mix? We use both CPU fallback and GPU for latency-sensitive ops.
00:02:52 - Ravi: Typical mix: 4x A100-80GB or 8x H100 per pool depends on model and batch size. For Llama-3-70b quantized, A100 80GB can handle X tokens/sec 
let me not handwave numbers, I'll run a capacity calc after this. We often recommend a mix of a baseline reserved pool sized for 95p SLO and a couple of warm standby nodes for fast burst.
00:03:11 - Maria: Do you support quantized model variants and kernel selection? We saw issues with some runtimes picking suboptimal kernels.
00:03:16 - Ravi: Yes, Redwood's runtime supports 4-bit/8-bit quantization-friendly execution paths and automatic kernel selection. We also provide a model catalog with verified performance profiles for each model+quantization combo.
00:03:27 - Avery: Thomas, can you share rough traffic shape? Is it steady or very spiky?
00:03:30 - Thomas: Mostly steady from 8am-6pm, with a spike batch job at 2am twice weekly for compliance reports. Spikes during business hours when campaigns run.
00:03:40 - Maria: Another constraint: we need audit logs down to the request level and key management via our KMS.
00:03:45 - Elaine: Yes, SOC2 required, SSO via SAML, RBAC for different teams, and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with HSM preferred.
00:03:52 - Ravi: Redwood Dedicated supports KMS integration and audit logs retention options. BYOK is available in Private deployments; for Dedicated we have KMS integrations and can integrate with customer-managed keys depending on contract. I'll attach our security doc.
00:04:06 - Maria: What's the difference between Dedicated and Private in practical terms? We want the same API surface but with more control.
00:04:12 - Avery: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools hosted by Redwood with network isolation and VPC peering. Private gives you a private control plane and optional on-prem package 
more control over networking and keys, useful for regulated workloads. Both provide the same API.
00:04:24 - Thomas: For Dedicated, is the control plane multi-tenant? We want to ensure no config drift or noisy neighbor issues.
00:04:30 - Ravi: The control plane in Dedicated is a customer-tenant setup; orchestration is multi-tenant but compute is isolated. We provide performance guarantees via SLAs and can configure resource reservations and QoS to avoid noisy neighbors.
00:04:43 - Maria: Cost 
how do pricing and committed capacity work? We have strict budget cycles.
00:04:47 - Avery: Pricing for Dedicated is typically a committed monthly GPU fee plus usage for burst. We can show modeled costs for different reserved pool sizes and burst allowances. We'll send a sample SOW with options (monthly commit tiers).
00:05:00 - Thomas: Any support for autoscaling? We don't want to overcommit but need predictable tails.
00:05:04 - Ravi: Yes, autoscaling policies can be conservative for Dedicated 
you can set minimum reserved capacity and maximum cap for burst. There's also warm standby nodes and rapid scale policies that keep KV cache warm to reduce cold-start tail.
00:05:17 - Maria: How does KV cache warm-up work across nodes? We have multi-region traffic, and cache miss rates kill latencies.
00:05:22 - Ravi: Redwood supports prefix and KV caching; cache warmups can be orchestrated with sticky routing or preloading. For multi-region, we recommend regional pools with smart routing by latency and cost, and a caching tier that can be shared via a replicated KV store. There are tradeoffs, we'll detail in the follow-up.
00:05:36 - Elaine: Encryption at rest 
we need to ensure model weights and logs are encrypted with customer keys.
00:05:41 - Ravi: On Private deployments, BYOK+HSM is standard. For Dedicated, we support envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS where available. Logs can be shipped to your SIEM via secure forwarding.
00:05:52 - Maria: Can we run a benchmark with our real traffic?
00:05:55 - Avery: Absolutely. Typical path: share sample payloads and traffic shapes, we run a benchmark on a matching Dedicated pool, and provide detailed token-level latency and cost breakdown. That will validate the sizing.
00:06:06 - Thomas: We'd like to include our 2am report spike in the benchmark. Also, can Redwood simulate failure or node drain to see graceful degradation?
00:06:13 - Ravi: Yes, we can run chaos scenarios: node drains, AZ failures, fallback to smaller model variants. Redwood's smart routing can fallback to cheaper model variants to keep service online during capacity constraints.
00:06:25 - Maria: About model variants 
can we pin versions and do canary rollouts? We need stable behavior for customer-facing flows.
00:06:31 - Avery: Yes, rollouts with canaries and A/B testing are supported in Console. You can pin model versions per route and set automatic fallbacks.
00:06:38 - Elaine: What about data residency? Some PII must stay in EU. We have branches in EU and NA.
00:06:43 - Ravi: Redwood has region controls; Dedicated pools can be provisioned in EU-only regions. For strict residency, Private on-prem is an option.
00:06:51 - Thomas: SLA questions 
what uptime and latency SLAs do you offer for Dedicated?
00:06:56 - Avery: We have SLA tiers: 99.9% uptime for Dedicated standard, higher tiers with financial credits for enterprise contracts. Latency SLOs are set per-model and per-deployment; we'll propose SLOs aligned with your requirements.
00:07:08 - Maria: Any recommended GPU count for our baseline 150 QPS with Llama-3-70b quantized?
00:07:13 - Ravi: Ballpark: for quantized 70b 4-bit on A100-80GB, a single GPU can do roughly 30-60 QPS depending on prompt length and batching. So baseline 150 QPS implies 3-6 GPUs reserved for core latency SLO, with warm standby for burst. I'll provide exact numbers after running tests with your prompts.
00:07:30 - Thomas: How long to provision Dedicated resources?
00:07:33 - Avery: Depending on region and quota, provisioning baseline Dedicated pool typically takes 1-2 weeks for standard setups; private/on-prem takes longer due to networking and install. If you need quick POC we can run hosted benchmarks in days.
00:07:45 - Maria: What's the handoff to our infra team for VPC peering? We need a checklist.
00:07:49 - Ravi: We'll share a VPC peering checklist and network diagram. It includes IP ranges, firewall rules, peering setup, and route tables. Also SAML SSO setup guidance.
00:07:58 - Elaine: For compliance docs, can you share SOC2 report and penetration test summary?
00:08:02 - Avery: Yes, we'll share SOC2 Type II and pen test summaries under NDA. Also our architecture whitepaper for Dedicated and Private.
00:08:10 - Maria: Any concerns about model drift or quality regressions when we update models or quantization?
00:08:15 - Ravi: Redwood Optimize offers quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to eval sets. We can integrate your evals to guard against regressions during rollouts.
00:08:24 - Thomas: Are there observability hooks 
 tracing, per-token cost, and latency breakdown?
00:08:28 - Avery: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, and distributed tracing integrations you can ship to your existing APM.
00:08:37 - Maria: For the benchmark, can you output a CSV with per-request latency and token breakdown?
00:08:41 - Ravi: Absolutely. We output raw logs, aggregated stats, and a benchmark spreadsheet with cost modeling.
00:08:47 - Elaine: A couple more policy questions 
can we set retention windows for logs and transcripts? We need 7-year retention for certain audit trails.
00:08:54 - Ravi: Retention is configurable; for Dedicated we can configure long-term retention and export to your archive buckets if needed. We'll match your legal retention policy in the SOW.
00:09:03 - Maria: If we start with Dedicated and later want Private on-prem, is migration supported?
00:09:08 - Avery: Yes, we support migration paths. The API and config layer are consistent, so you can migrate models and rollout policies. There will be work to move keys and configure networking.
00:09:17 - Thomas: Any immediate blockers from our side?
00:09:20 - Maria: We need pricing modeled against our budget. Also Elaine needs to review the SOC2 and KMS options.
00:09:25 - Elaine: I'll need a security questionnaire and the SOC2 artifacts.
00:09:28 - Avery: We'll send those. Proposed next steps: 1) Avery sends pricing + SOW, 2) Maria shares sample prompts & traffic, 3) Ravi runs capacity calc and schedules benchmark with Thomas.
00:09:41 - Thomas: Sounds good. Can we aim for benchmark the week of 9/14?
00:09:44 - Ravi: Yes, if we have sample payloads by 9/4 we can prep infra and run between 9/14-9/18.
00:09:50 - Maria: One last thing 
latency budget breakdown per component? We need to see target for network + runtime + model inference.
00:09:57 - Ravi: We'll provide typical breakdowns and you can adjust based on your network path. For short prompts, model inference usually dominates, so GPU choice matters.
00:10:07 - Avery: Any other questions?
00:10:09 - Elaine: On access controls, can we have role separation between dev and prod teams?
00:10:12 - Ravi: Yes, RBAC is supported 
fine-grained roles in Console and SAML groups mapping.
00:10:18 - Maria: Okay great. Thanks everyone.
00:10:21 - Avery: Thanks 
 we'll follow up with the pricing, security docs, and benchmark plan.
00:10:25 - Thomas: Appreciate it.
00:10:27 - Elaine: Thank you.
